title: Ops staff playback — cross-leads weekly
content:
Meeting: Cross-team ops staff playback — weekly
Date: 2027-04-06
Time: 09:30–10:45 PT
Facilitator: Ayesha Patel (platform eng lead)
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (serving runtime), Mei Chen (SRE), Javier Morales (private deploys), Noor Ahmed (dedicated), Priya Rao (console), several leads dialed in for 10–20 min blocks

Purpose: rapid cross-team sync to highlight material risks, unblock cross-domain work, and capture concrete follow-ups. Focus this week on the canary regression, Dedicated capacity headroom, and upcoming maintenance window.

1) Quick signal check (3-min each)
- Serving runtime (Liam): Canary rollout of model-serving v2.3 at 10% progressed to 7% — seeing elevated P99 token latency on long-context flows (~+120ms). Initial hypothesis: degraded KV cache eviction under heavy prefix churn.
- SRE (Mei): Incident report on API throttling last Friday — root cause was a misapplied rate-limit policy during a deploy (ops rule ENG-4821). Postmortem draft ready, expecting exec summary by Friday. MTTR metrics: median 18m, one customer observed 40m.
- Private deployments (Javier): Two pilot installs completed for EU-regulated customer; installer issues with KMS rotated keys in 1 of 2 clusters. Workaround documented; full fix targeted for 2027-04-12.
- Dedicated (Noor): Pool utilization creeping toward committed cap in us-west region — forecasting 87% utilization during next marketing spike (w/in 10 days). Exploring short-term burst quota and longer-term slot increases.
- Console (Priya): New rollouts UI shipped to internal alpha; flag toggles for canary policies present but need cross-check with routing layer to prevent mismatch.

2) Deep dive: Canary latency regression (Liam, 20 min)
Summary: v2.3 brings aggressive KV compression and a kernel scheduling tweak. Under synthetic long-prefix workloads we see 10–12% P99 latency increase for sequences >2k tokens. Production signal shows subset of traffic hitting coupled eviction path.
Notes:
- Repro steps captured in github issue linked at https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/issues/2319
- Immediate mitigation options discussed: rollback to v2.2, reduce canary to 3% and isolate heavy-prefix customers, disable kernel scheduling tweak via runtime flag.
Decision (temp): Pause further canary expansion. Roll back the kernel scheduling tweak in the next hotfix (target: 2027-04-08). Keep v2.3 on 7% for telemetry purposes but route known heavy-prefix customers to v2.2.
Action items:
- Liam: prepare rollback hotfix branch and PR, target merge by 2027-04-07 (JIRA-ENG-4821).
- Mei + SRE: add a synthetic test that reproduces prefix churn pattern in staging (target 2027-04-09).

3) Capacity and committed usage (Noor, 10 min)
- Short-term: request for 15% burst pool for 72 hours around projected marketing event. Finance needs estimate.
- Long-term: proposal to increase committed slots in us-west by 20% starting next billing cycle; requires contract update.
Action items:
- Noor: create capacity request doc and cost delta estimate, loop in finance (due 2027-04-08).
- Ayesha: raise to GTM leadership for approval if delta > $15k/mo (by 2027-04-09).

4) Private deployments blockers (Javier, 8 min)
- KMS rotation bug: installer fails when customer uses HSM-backed keys with nonstandard alias. Repro and workaround documented.
Decision: ship patch in 2-step release: hotfix to unblock current pilots (2027-04-12), followed by full installer refactor for edge cases (Q2 milestone).
Action items:
- Javier: hotfix PR and smoke test checklist (due 2027-04-11).
- Devops: schedule one maintenance window for pilots (2027-04-13 02:00–04:00 UTC), customer notified.

5) Observability & cost signals (Priya + Mei, 10 min)
- Observability team rolled out token-level cost telemetry to alpha customers. Early signal: small proportion of routes are 30% of cost due to repeated long-context reruns.
- Suggestion: add route-level sampling to detect expensive queries and a cost-alert threshold.
Action items:
- Priya: prototype route-level sampling dashboard and link to runbook (due 2027-04-15).
- Mei: add cost spike alert to SRE playbook (JIRA-OPS-4980) and test during next synthetic load.

6) Incident review highlights (Mei, 10 min)
- Root cause: human error in rate-limit config during rolling deploy (config push applied to prod without guardrail).
- Short-term: enable deploy-time policy checks; longer-term: policy-as-code + canary enforcement.
Decisions:
- Immediate: add pre-deploy lint for rate limit policies in CI (target 2027-04-14).
- Longer-term: integrate policy-as-code into release pipeline (Q2 OKR).
Action items:
- Mei + Release Eng: implement CI lint job and add to pre-deploy gating (due 2027-04-14).

7) Cross-team operational asks & unresolved questions (rapid-fire)
- Rollouts UI parity: does routing layer honor all new flags? (Priya) -> Noor to confirm mapping (due 2027-04-09).
- SLA metric: clarify how Dedicated commit violations are logged vs customer-visible alerts (Noor) -> Mei to propose an audit view (due 2027-04-12).
- Model quantization recommendation: can Optimize team provide guidance for 8-bit baseline vs mixed-int8 for latency-sensitive workloads? (Liam) -> Action: ping Optimize team, request short advisory (due 2027-04-13).

8) Risks and exec summary (2 min)
- Key risk: If canary regression not contained, risk of wider customer impact and SLA breaches during marketing spike.
- Ask for exec visibility: need $ approval for short-term burst capacity and sign-off on rolling hotfix plan.

9) Parking lot / FYI (items to track outside meeting)
- Internal alpha: rollouts UI testcases and cross-check matrix (Priya).
- Convergence workshop: invite Model Ops and Optimize to next week for quantization decisions.
- Hiring note: platform-engineering headcount request for Q3 ramp — submit by 2027-04-20.

Decisions summary (one-liners):
- Pause canary expansion for v2.3; hotfix to revert scheduling tweak (owner: Liam, due 2027-04-08).
- Burst capacity request to handle upcoming marketing spike (owner: Noor, due 2027-04-08).
- CI lint job for rate-limit policies added to pre-deploy gating (owner: Mei + Release Eng, due 2027-04-14).
- Hotfix for KMS installer issue (owner: Javier, due 2027-04-11).

Action item table (compact):
- Liam: rollback hotfix PR for v2.3 scheduling tweak (JIRA-ENG-4821) — 2027-04-07
- Mei: synthetic prefix churn test + CI lint job for rate limits (JIRA-OPS-4980) — 2027-04-09 / 2027-04-14
- Noor: capacity request + finance estimate — 2027-04-08
- Javier: KMS hotfix PR + maintenance window scheduling — 2027-04-11
- Priya: route-level sampling dashboard — 2027-04-15

Next meeting: 2027-04-13 09:30 PT (focus: post-hotfix telemetry, capacity decision, quantization advisory)

Notes to recipients: please update the linked JIRA tickets and Confluence post (CONFL-1287) as progress is made. If you cannot meet the stated due dates, ping Ayesha with revised ETA.

Raw transcript fragments and side-channel notes (informal):
- Liam: "we saw the knee in P99 only when prefix churn > 500 unique prefixes/min"
- Mei: "policy linting would have caught the bad config; feasible to short-circuit this in CI"
- Javier: "installer logs are noisy — need standard schema for KMS errors"
- Noor: "if we don't secure burst slots now, we'll hit headroom on the first peak day"

End of notes.

Document version: working draft — will update after hotfix lands and SRE confirms synthetic test results.
